This vignette covers the last mile of the preparation workflow: what
exactly to upload, how to package supplementary files, and — so there
are no surprises — what happens to your files once TRIA receives them.
It assumes you have already been through `vignette("workflow")` and have
a complete `QWAmetadata` object and `QWAdata` files (and, optionally,
a validated zip of supplementary files) ready on disk.

---

## What to submit

A submission consists of:

1. **`{dataset_name}_QWAmetadata.json`** — written with
   [write_QWAmetadata()].
2. **`{dataset_name}_QWAcells.csv(.gz)`** and
   **`{dataset_name}_QWArings.csv(.gz)`** — written with
   [write_QWAdata()].
3. Optionally, **one zip archive of supplementary resources** — original
   and annotated images, raw ROXAS / ROXAS AI output, reference series,
   etc. (see `vignette("resources")`).

To hand over these three (or four) files, email
[tria@wsl.ch](mailto:tria@wsl.ch) and either:

- share a link to them on a file transfer service of your choice (e.g.
  Dropbox, Google Drive, your institution's own service) — whatever you
  already use is fine; or
- ask for an invite link to WSL's file transfer server, if you'd rather
  not set one up yourself.

### Packaging supplementary resources

Gather every supplementary file you want to submit into a **single
directory** (nesting subfolders as preferred — e.g. per tree or slide),
run `add_resources()`/`compile_resources()` on it, and resolve anything
flagged `"review"` — see `vignette("resources")` for the full workflow —
before zipping that directory for upload.

Doing this yourself first means naming problems (an unrecognised file, a
missing `linked_label`) surface on your end, where you can still rename
or annotate things, rather than during our ingestion checks. We re-run
`compile_resources()` on our side regardless, pointed directly at your
uploaded zip. If you provide a `$resources` manifest, it's trusted as
ground truth for anything it lists that's still in the zip; if the zip is
missing a file the manifest expects (anything not already marked
`"ignore"`), that's treated as a real inconsistency and ingestion stops
until it's resolved. Extra files in the zip the manifest doesn't mention
are left out rather than guessed at. If you don't provide a manifest, we
build one from scratch the same way `compile_resources()` would for you.

---

## What happens after you submit

We make a small number of server-side adjustments to your files during
ingestion, so that what ends up in the TRIA database differs slightly
from what you uploaded. None of these require any action on your part —
they're listed here purely so the shape of the final record isn't a
surprise.

### `QWAcells.csv`

Derived cell measurements (`tca`, `rwd2`, `dcwt`, `cwtall_adj`, `cdrad`,
`cdtan`, `cdratio`, `sector100` — added via [complete_measures()]) are
**removed**. They are trivially recomputed from the raw measurements, so 
we don't store a second, potentially stale copy.

### `QWAmetadata.json`

| Field | Change | When |
|---|---|---|
| `$dataset$ds_access` | Removed | On ingestion |
| `$dataset$citation` | Added (includes the newly minted DOI if the dataset is made public) | On ingestion |
| `$dataset$version` | Added | On ingestion |
| `$dataset$doi` | Added | When the dataset is registered / made public |
| `$images[*].fname_image`, `fname_cells`, `fname_rings`, `fname_settings` | Removed | On ingestion |
| `$resources[*].fname_resource` | Removed | On ingestion |
| `$resources` | Checked against the uploaded archive (see [Packaging supplementary resources] above); storage key added | On ingestion |

The `fname_*` / `fname_resource` columns hold absolute paths from your
own machine — meaningful while you're preparing the data, meaningless
(and potentially revealing local file-system structure) once archived,
so they are always stripped rather than carried into the database.
